The installer handles everything: uv, Python 3.11, Node.js, ripgrep, ffmpeg, and a portable Git Bash (MinGit, unpacked to %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\git — no admin required, completely isolated from any system Git install). Hermes uses this bundled Git Bash to run shell commands.

Android / Termux: The tested manual path is documented in the Termux guide.

Windows: Native Windows is fully supported — the PowerShell one-liner above installs everything. If you'd rather use WSL2, the Linux command works there too. Native Windows install lives under %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes, WSL2 installs under ~/.hermes as on Linux.
Windows Defender or antivirus flags uv.exe as malware
If your antivirus (Bitdefender, Windows Defender, etc.) quarantines uv.exe from the Hermes bin folder (%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\bin\uv.exe), this is a false positive.

The file is Astral's uv — the Rust Python package manager Hermes bundles to manage its Python environment. ML-based antivirus engines commonly flag unsigned Rust binaries that download and install packages.

In SAP BTP, you don’t assign a subaccount to a user — rather, you add users as members of a subaccount and grant them permissions via role collections. Here’s how:
You need the Subaccount Administrator role collection on the target subaccount.
The user must exist in a trusted identity provider (SAP ID Service, SAP Cloud Identity Services, or another configured IdP).
Step 1 — Add the user to the subaccount
Open the SAP BTP Cockpit and navigate to your subaccount.
In the left navigation, go to Security → Users.
Enter the user’s User Name (usually their email) and E-Mail.
The user is now a subaccount member, but has no permissions yet.
Step 2 — Assign a role collection to the user
Go to Security → Users and select the user.
In the Role Collections panel on the right, click Assign Role Collection.
Select the relevant role collection(s) (e.g., Subaccount Administrator, service-specific roles).
Open the target role collection and click Edit.
Under the Users section, enter the user’s email and select the identity provider.
